message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for binary classification problems. Unlike linear regression, which predicts continuous outcomes, logistic regression models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes (e.g., “yes” vs. “no”). It does this by applying the logistic (sigmoid) function to a linear combination of the input features, producing an output between 0 and 1 that can be interpreted as a probability. The model is typically trained by maximizing the likelihood of the observed data (or equivalently minimizing cross‑entropy loss). Once trained, logistic regression can be used to predict class labels or probabilities for new observations.
